# ethereum-optimism/ecosystem Weekly Report (Feb 22 - 28, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week’s activity focused on refining protocol stability and infrastructure reliability within the OP Stack. Key technical discussions centered on the `op-batcher`'s handling of post-Holocene ordering and defining Service Level Agreements (SLAs) for the `op-supernode`. While development included routine dependency maintenance, the primary focus remained on resolving architectural edge cases in concurrent batching and improving the robustness of RPC performance monitoring.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### Dependency Management & Maintenance
Efforts were made to keep the ecosystem's underlying libraries secure and up to date.
*   **Library Updates:** A pull request was submitted to update the `bn.js` dependency from version 4.12.2 to 4.12.3 ([#977](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/pull/977)), ensuring the project benefits from the latest upstream fixes in big number arithmetic.

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Closed Issues
*   **RPC Performance:** The team addressed reports regarding `eth_getLogs` memory exhaustion. Issue [#769](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/769) was identified as a duplicate of existing performance tracking ([#768](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/768)) and closed to consolidate troubleshooting efforts.

### Active Issues & Technical Discussions
*   **op-batcher Post-Holocene Ordering:** Significant attention is being paid to `op-batcher` behavior in concurrent mode. Discussion on [#18507](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/18507) highlights a failure to account for specific ordering requirements introduced in the Holocene upgrade. This work is currently being tracked alongside a related pull request in the core optimism repository.
*   **op-supernode SLA Definitions:** There is an ongoing architectural debate regarding the `Superroot` object's SLA ([#19180](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/19180)). The current consensus leans toward treating Optimistic Roots as a "best-attempt" effort, where unavailable roots are either excluded or represented by empty values to prevent system stalls.

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
Collaboration this week was characterized by cross-repository coordination, particularly between the ecosystem and core protocol teams. The link between issue [#18507](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/18507) and external PRs suggests a highly integrated development workflow. Contributors like `kien-rise` and `axelKingsley` are actively driving the technical specifications for Superchain infrastructure, ensuring that protocol upgrades like Holocene are correctly implemented across all batching and node components.
